_comment: Weights are relative (any positive numbers). 'metrics' measure the QB's own production in games he STARTED. 'context' measures the help around him; a QB with a WEAKER supporting cast gets credit, a stronger one gets docked. 'weapon_parts' sets how the Weapons grade itself is built. 'context' also includes defenses faced: a tougher schedule earns credit. Set any weight to 0 to ignore it.

run_game.label: Run Game
run_game._parts: non-QB rushing EPA/carry, yards/carry, RB rush yards over expected

pass_pro.label: Pass protection
pass_pro._parts: O-line: pressures, sacks, hits, hurries per dropback (adjusted for time to throw and blitzes) + time to throw; see pass_pro_parts

opp_defense.label: Defenses faced
opp_defense._parts: pass defenses in his starts, each rated on its games BEFORE that week (see 'defense')

without_qb._comment: How his pass catchers played in games he missed, judged only on what receivers control (getting open, YAC, production after removing the backup's accuracy). Share of his weapons grade = max_share * games_missed / (games_missed + prior_games). Set max_share to 0 to turn off.

defense._comment: How pass defenses are rated going into each game: what opposing QBs did against them in earlier weeks. Last season's rating counts as 'prior_games' games so week 1 isn't blank.

missing_players._comment: Who missed each game comes from snap counts. Key weapon = at least key_weapon_min_share % of team targets; his targets go to a backup graded replacement_grade (weekly rankings). Key defenders = each defense's top key_defenders players; losing all of them makes the defense defense_impact std devs weaker (weekly and season rankings).
